messages:
arya: Hi team  newbie here (start 2026-09-15). Quick mix of questions: 1) my benefits portal shows effective 2026-10-01 so ER visit on 2026-09-20 wasn’t covered  can I request retro or company reimbursement? 2) I’m an international hire and my bank uses IBAN (EU). How do reimbursements get paid? 3) Do I need to update any tax forms for non-resident status? cc @lisa @tom-payroll :wave:
benefits-bot: Enrollment received. Carrier effective date: 2026-10-01. For services before the effective date, submit itemized receipts to Expensify under category `healthcare-reimbursements` for a retro review. See: https://redwood.intranet/benefits/reimbursements :link:
lisa: Welcome Aria (and congrats!). Short: upload the ER receipt + discharge summary to Expensify and open a People Ops ticket asking for a retro review. We do carrier submissions first; if denied we may process a discretionary reimbursement. Please redact any full SSNs and full card numbers.
arya: Thanks  for Expensify description, should I list patient as "self" and include diagnosis? I’m also worried about sending US-style medical docs from abroad (they have sensitive IDs).
julia-hr: For privacy, redact clinical notes and IDs; keep provider name, date of service, amount, and service description. Put patient as "employee: Aria" or "self". If the provider refuses to itemize, a signed provider statement works.
tom-payroll: On payment: we can pay reimbursements to a US bank ACH or as an international wire. For wires to IBANs, we need a vendor form + bank letter verifying account holder and IBAN. If you prefer, we can issue a USD-denominated international ACH/wire; fees may apply. To avoid fees, many international hires open a US-based fintech USD account and use ACH. If you want a wire, attach the completed vendor onboarding form in the PO ticket.
arya: Got it. Which vendor form? Is there a quick template? Also when would reimbursement hit my account if carrier approves?
lisa: Use the vendor form here: https://redwood.intranet/payroll/vendor-onboard. For timing: if carrier approves, benefits processes the vendor payment and it typically hits the next vendor run (7-10 business days). If we do an internal discretionary payment, payroll processes it as a separate vendor/payment run as soon as approvals are done (can be same cycle if docs in by cutoff).
arya: And the tax question  I filled a W-4 but I’m non-resident for tax purposes this year. Should I submit a different form?
tom-payroll: Good question. Non-resident aliens generally submit Form W-4 but may need to indicate treaty benefits or different withholding; we also require Form 8233 or a treaty claim depending on circumstances. Payroll will reach out for country-specific docs. Please DM me your country and visa type and I’ll confirm required paperwork. Also note: reimbursements processed as qualified plan reimbursements (carrier-approved) are non-taxable; discretionary reimbursements may be taxable depending on treatment.
benefits-bot: Reminder: copy-paste Expensify memo template. Also tag your report with `new-hire-international` if you need vendor wire payment.

Expensify memo suggestion (copy/paste):
```
Provider: St. Luke International ER
Date of service: 2026-09-20
Service: ER visit, observation
Amount: $540.00
Patient: Aria (employee)
Category: healthcare-reimbursements
Attachments: itemized bill, discharge summary (redacted IDs)
Notes: New-hire retro request. Benefits effective 2026-10-01. Please escalate to benefits admin for carrier review. If carrier denies, request discretionary reimbursement and international vendor onboarding for IBAN wire.
```
arya: Uploading ER bill now (Expensify ER-44221) and opened ticket PO-5229. I attached the vendor form in case we need a wire. Thanks all :pray:
lisa: I see PO-5229  I’ll route to benefits admin and flag payroll for potential wire. Note for payroll: vendor form + passport copy required for international vendor setup. tom-payroll, assigning to you to confirm any tax docs.
tom-payroll: Got it  I’ll DM Aria for country/visa and confirm whether Form 8233 or other docs are needed. Also will confirm wire/fee policy in the ticket. If you want faster cash, request a payroll advance in the ticket and mark `medical_advance`; payroll can approve same-day in urgent cases and recover over future paychecks.
arya: Ideal is carrier pays but happy to request an advance if needed. Appreciate the help everyone! :smile:
